Subject: Re: Request — Redwood demo (Calendly timezones acting up)

Hi Liz — thanks for the note and the preferred windows. Sorry about the confusion; Calendly normally auto-detects based on browser locale, but a couple of things can override that (company SSO, certain proxy headers, or if someone opens the link from a calendar client).

Workarounds that typically fix this quickly:
- On the Calendly booking page there is a small "Time zone" dropdown above the slots (below the date picker). Click "See other time zones" and select Australia/Brisbane or Australia/Sydney.
- If that still shows incorrectly, append a timezone query parameter to the link — e.g. https://calendly.com/redwood/demo?timezone=Australia/Sydney — which forces the view. (Not all Calendly plans support all query params; Jonas can set a canonical fallback link for our team.)
- Short-term: I attached an ICS with explicit TZ definitions for the slot I think will work based on your list. Import that into your calendar and it should show correctly for both Brisbane and Sydney.

Because your attendees span QLD (no DST) and NSW (DST), I'll propose an approach below that avoids ambiguity. If you'd prefer, Marissa (our solutions engineer) can host a quick 10m sync to confirm sign-ups and ensure the right invite lands on both calendars.

Proposed: Tue 20 Nov 2028 at 02:00 UTC (which is 13:00 AEST / 14:00 AEDT) — I included the ICS for that slot. If that doesn't work we'll pick one of your other windows.

Attaching: redwood_demo_proposed.ics (explicit TZ)

Cheers,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
tessa.morgan@redwood.com

The ICS you attached looks better on my end and shows the right hour for Brisbane. Two quick questions: 
1) For multi-region attendees, what's the recommended line in the invite title? (e.g. "Redwood demo — 13:00 AEST / 14:00 AEDT")
2) Will adding the ICS create duplicate slots for other attendees who use the Calendly link later? We want to avoid double-booking.

If you can send a calendar invite created in UTC with local-times in the body, that'll be safest for our team — then our scheduling address will accept it and we can distribute internally.

Appreciate the help.

Liz

Subject: Re: Request — Redwood demo (Calendly timezones acting up)

Hi Liz — great, glad the ICS helped. Short answers and actions below.

1) Invite title: we recommend including both UTC and a clear localized label for attendees. Example: "Redwood demo — 02:00 UTC / 13:00 AEST (Brisbane) / 14:00 AEDT (Sydney)". That removes ambiguity for cross-region teams.

2) Duplicates: importing an ICS is a separate calendar event — it won't reserve the Calendly slot unless someone books on Calendly; to avoid double-booking we can either:
   - create the event centrally in UTC and send it as an invite (what you asked for), OR
   - reserve the Calendly slot first and then send out the confirmed invite.

I've created a single UTC-based invite and attached it (final_invite_utc.ics) — it contains VTIMEZONE blocks for Brisbane and Sydney and a short body listing local conversions. Please import or accept the invite from scheduling@clearpath.com when you get it.

Jonas: can you follow up and add a fallback Calendly URL (or a Chili Piper redirect) that forces "viewer timezone" detection and logs the detected timezone to HubSpot? That'll reduce these proxy/SO issues for future bookings.

Marissa: happy to run the quick 10m if you want to walk through one invite flow with their scheduling address.

Liz — let me know once scheduling@clearpath.com accepts the invite and I'll mark the HubSpot record accordingly.

Thanks,
Tessa
